parole.testo: Uncertain. Perhaps ultimately from Kimbundu marimbondo, plural of rimbondo (“Sceliphron spirifex, a bright yellow and black wasp”), possibly via Portuguese marimbondo. Compare Sranan Tongo marbonsu (“wasp of the genus Polistes”).

parole.testo: From the pronunciation of African slaves, of unknown ultimate origin. Possibly a corruption of bandore (from Spanish bandurria), alternatively from a West African language such as Mandinka banjul, or Kimbundu mbanza.

parole.significato: A toasted manioc flour used in Brazilian cookery, typically as an accompaniment to a main meal.
parole.testo: From Portuguese farofa, perhaps from Kimbundu falofa or from Latin far (“a type of hulled wheat”) + offa (“chunk; dumpling”).

parole.significato: A fortified residence or encampment in Angola, or the military power associated with it.
parole.testo: From Portuguese quilombo, and its source Kimbundu kilombo (“refuge, encampment”).
